entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Fu Jian, courtesy name Yonggu or Wenyu, was the third monarch of the Di-led Chinese Former Qin dynasty, ruling as Heavenly King from 386 to 385. Under his reign, Fu Jian unified Northern China by conquering several key territories, including the Former Yan, Chouchi, and Dai states, until he was defeated at the Battle of Fei River in 383. The defeat led to the disintegration of the Former Qin state.

Fu Jian's legacy is complex, marked by both significant military victories and ultimately, his downfall. His unification of Northern China had a lasting impact on the region, but his brief reign also left a power vacuum that other warlords would later exploit.

The fall of the former Qin dynasty was a pivotal moment in Chinese history, marking the end of one era and the beginning of another. Fu Jian's story serves as a reminder of the cyclical nature of history, where even the greatest leaders can fall victim to their own hubris or external forces beyond their control.

Fu Jian is remembered today for his bravery and strategic prowess on the battlefield, but also for his inability to sustain power in the face of overwhelming opposition. His legacy continues to fascinate historians and scholars, offering a glimpse into the complexities of leadership and the fleeting nature of human achievement.

entities.summary: Fu Jian, courtesy name Yonggu (永固) or Wenyu (文玉), also known by his posthumous name as the Emperor Xuanzhao of Former Qin (前秦宣昭帝), was the third monarch of the Di-led Chinese Former Qin dynasty, ruling as Heavenly King. Under his reign, the Former Qin unified Northern China by conquering the Former Yan, Chouchi, Former Liang, and Dai, as well as the Eastern Jin's Yi Province, until he was repelled at the Battle of Fei River in 383. Following this defeat, the Former Qin state disintegrated and Fu was assassinated in 385 by Yao Chang, his former subordinate who then founded the Later Qin dynasty.
